newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco expects strong agricultural output.
newsitem.headline: Morocco expects strong agricultural output.

text.p: Morocco expects a good agricultural year despite heavy winter rains that hampered plantings, a senior official at the Agriculture ministry said on Tuesday.
A total of 4.5 million hectares were sown to autumn wheat and barley, he said.
Areas that were not planted because of the poor weather would be devoted to spring crops such as sunflower and maize.
Because of heavy rains in November and December, floods had hit nearly 20,000 hectares of cereals and sugar, mainly in the rich farming areas of Gharb and Loukkos in the north, an analyst said.
No official forecast for this year's output was immediately available.
But the Casablanca-based Centre Marocain de Conjoncture earlier predicted that Morocco would produce 7.0 to 8.0 million tonnes of cereals.
The agriculture ministry earlier forecast a total of 5.6 million hectares sown for all crops, similar to the area last year. Almost 900,000 hectares are located in irrigated areas.
Morocco harvested a record 10 million tonnes of cereals last year after a severe drought reduced 1995 output to 1.6 million tonnes, the Statistics Directorate said in a recent, revised report.
